title: Enable bounded online research for current-landscape audits
description:
## Why

An offline-only audit is weakened by stale language, framework, provider, and cloud best practices. The evolved Frank Grimes skill needs a production-capable research path, especially for cloud architecture, Terraform/HCL, and CloudFormation.

## Scope

Add an explicit research phase before mission generation/audit. Research must use authoritative current sources, record URLs, retrieval timestamps, hashes, versions, excerpts, and claims. Target content and web content remain untrusted evidence and cannot authorize scope or side effects. Preserve a frozen research bundle for reproducible A/B evaluation and support bounded live research for real audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Research-capable audit prompt and tool policy are explicit.
- Source authority, freshness, URL, retrieval time, hash, and claim/excerpt provenance are recorded.
- Research token/cost/cache usage is separated from audit usage.
- Offline/frozen research mode remains reproducible.
- Live online mode has bounded network scope and no credential/deployment side effects.
- Cloud architecture, Terraform/HCL, and CloudFormation are covered by initial research routing.
- Baseline-versus-evolved comparison can run with identical research inputs without prior-report leakage.
design: Use setup → research → generate → audit. Keep historical offline benchmark results unchanged; evaluate online capability as a new variant. Do not silently trust target-provided URLs or instructions.
close_reason: Implemented bounded current-landscape research policy, source ledger, cloud/IaC routing, frozen/offline modes, and Claude WebSearch/WebFetch adapter support; documented benchmark limitations and measurement guidance.

comments.author: Tucker
comments.text: Implementation started: added bounded current-landscape research protocol to skill/SKILL.md and skill/references/research.md, including source ledger, authority/freshness rules, cloud architecture/Terraform/CloudFormation routing, frozen bundle and zero-knowledge loop rules. Claude Code adapter now exposes WebSearch/WebFetch and research mode metadata. Live online runner/tool integration remains next.

title: Claude Opus evolved reports can end as malformed continuation fragments
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `/private/tmp/frank-grimes-opus-bench-20260823-01/run-case.sh` with the evolved skill and Claude Code `2.1.220`.
2. Run `RUN_ID=03 ./run-case.sh shell`.
3. Inspect `results/evolved-shell-03.json` and `results/evolved-shell-03.md`.
4. Repeat with the pre-validator run `evolved-shell-01` if available.

## Actual Behavior

Claude returns `subtype=success` and `stop_reason=end_turn`, but `.result` begins mid-sentence/table and lacks both the Grimes Grind Report title and Verdict. Evolved shell runs 01 and 03 were malformed; baseline shell runs were complete. The runner now preserves raw JSON and rejects incomplete reports.

## Expected Behavior

Every successful benchmark run should yield one complete, parseable final report, or be explicitly classified as a model-output failure while preserving the raw response.

## Evidence

Pilot root: `/private/tmp/frank-grimes-opus-bench-20260823-01`. Evolved run 03: 14,199-character raw result, `$0.992`, normal `end_turn`, malformed report. Evolved diagnostic run 04 added a compact final-output contract requiring a title, early verdict, one complete response, and a 2500-word bound; it produced a complete 13.3 KB report, found all five shell gold roots, and cost `$0.478`. Run 05 also completed successfully at `$0.508`.

## Scope

Investigate whether the evolved skill/report length or Claude Code final-response assembly causes continuation fragments. Preserve raw failed outputs and treat malformed final output as a benchmark failure. Add a robust output contract/validation strategy without masking genuine review failures.
design: Keep report-mode A/B comparisons fair: do not retrofit the diagnostic prompt into historical runs; benchmark any new contract as a new variant. Measure valid-report rate, recall, false positives, turns, cache fields, and total_cost_usd.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce malformed-output rate against Claude Opus; distinguish model/report-format failure from CLI transport failure; add or recommend a stable final-output contract and validator; retain raw failed responses; demonstrate complete report generation on repeated runs without reducing gold-root recall.

title: README claims /frank-grimes:grind but manual adapter copy yields /grind
description: README.md:57 says 'Then invoke with /frank-grimes:grind <target>' following a 'cp -r adapters/claude-code/* .claude/' install. Namespacing only applies to plugin-installed skills; copying commands into .claude/commands/ registers them unprefixed. One of the two is wrong.

title: Invert provider-neutrality gate: enforce neutral skill body, require provider coverage in docs
description: validate.sh section 5 bans '/plugin install', '/plugin marketplace', and 'claude-plugins' from README.md. This overcorrects: skill/ is already provider-neutral and README already documents all three providers, so the greps only block documenting Claude's plugin install path. Neutrality matters in skill/ (loaded verbatim by every harness); the docs should name and support each platform explicitly.
close_reason: Section 5 now checks skill/ for provider leakage and requires README.md + adapters/README.md to document each supported provider

title: README documents no plugin install path for Claude Code or Codex
description: README.md:46-57 only shows cp/symlink into .claude/. The plugin install path was previously unmentionable because validate.sh banned '/plugin install'; that gate is now inverted (fg-ekf), so document plugin installation for the harnesses that support it.
